sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Old Bridge, NJ?
sections.html:
Old Bridge Township is the largest of the four towns here, with 70,228 residents by the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, and a house sale there should start with a call to the township's Housing Inspection Division. Sellers can list, sell privately or take a cash offer, and each route runs into the same local and state paperwork before the deed is recorded.

The township covers 38.18 square miles of land in Middlesex County, about 25 miles from New York City across Raritan Bay from Staten Island. That is a lot of ground for a single municipality, so a street in Laurence Harbor, Madison Park or Brownville can feel very different from one near Route 9. Know which part of the township your house is in, because buyers shop by area.

sections.h2: How did Old Bridge Township get its shape?
sections.html:
The area was incorporated as Madison Township on March 2, 1869, when it separated from South Amboy Township. Voters changed the name to Old Bridge in a November 5, 1975 referendum, passing it 7,150 to 4,888, mainly to give the township a single postal designation and to avoid confusion with the borough of Madison in Morris County.

Farming, clay pits along Cheesequake Creek, snuff mills and an apple orchard and distillery dominated the early economy. The population was 7,366 in 1950 and 22,772 by 1960, then 48,715 by 1970, as developments replaced farms. That building boom is why much of the housing stock dates from the postwar decades, and why roofs, windows and heating systems are common repair items at sale.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Old Bridge housing?
sections.html:
Old Bridge is more affordable than Nutley or Ocean Township, with a median owner-occupied home value of $461,000 for 2020 through 2024. About 70 percent of households own, and 94.4 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, the highest figure among these four towns.

sections.h2: What does a sale involve with the Old Bridge Housing Inspection Division?
sections.html:
The township keeps a Housing Inspection Division with its own requirements page. Ask the division, before you list, whether a resale inspection applies to your address, and get the current checklist, the fee and the scheduling steps from it, because the township sets those details and can change them.

State fire rules add a second requirement. A one- or two-family house needs a certificate of smoke alarm compliance before it is sold, issued through the municipality and valid for six months. Ask the township which office issues the certificate for your address before you apply.

  • Close any open building permits before the inspection, since an open permit can hold up a municipal sign-off.
  • If you added a deck, finished a basement or replaced a furnace, locate the permit and final inspection records.
  • Replace dead smoke and carbon monoxide alarms before the visit.

If the house needs repairs a seller cannot afford, the township's Home Improvement Program offers funds to income-qualified households to correct health, safety and code conditions. Ask the township whether you qualify before choosing between repairs and an as-is sale.

sections.h2: Which parts of Old Bridge affect how a house sells?
sections.html:
The Census-designated places are Old Bridge itself, with 27,210 residents in 2020, Madison Park with 8,050, Laurence Harbor with 6,635 and Brownville with 2,383. Laurence Harbor has a 70-acre Raritan Bay beachfront with a boardwalk, playgrounds and fishing. Cheesequake State Park covers about 1,600 acres.

Waterfront and park proximity can help a listing, but bayfront and creek-side homes also draw questions about flood exposure. The township's streams include the South River, Matchaponix Brook, Deep Run and Cheesequake Creek. Gather your flood insurance history and elevation information before buyers ask.

Recent temperature records place Old Bridge in a humid subtropical climate, in hardiness zones 7a and 7b. Humid summers make basement moisture and attic ventilation points that buyers and inspectors check, so a dry, clean basement helps a listing.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools shape buyer demand in Old Bridge?
sections.html:
The Garden State Parkway crosses the township for about 1.9 miles and has Interchange 120, signed for Laurence Harbor and Matawan. U.S. Route 9 and Routes 18, 34 and 35 also run through it, plus county roads 516, 520, 527 and 615. The New Jersey Turnpike is reachable at Exit 9 in East Brunswick or Exit 8A in Monroe.

NJ Transit buses on Route 9 run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, Newark and Jersey City, and the Old Bridge Park and Ride sits on Route 9 northbound near Ernston Road. The nearest trains are the North Jersey Coast Line stops at Aberdeen-Matawan and South Amboy.

Old Bridge Township Public Schools run 14 schools and enrolled 8,096 students in 2022-23. Eleven are elementary schools, there are two middle schools, Jonas Salk and Carl Sandburg, and Old Bridge High School had 2,707 students. Middlesex County's magnet schools also take eighth graders from across the county.

sections.h2: What costs and deadlines should an Old Bridge seller plan for?
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. The Division of Taxation's own example puts it at $1,910 on a $325,000 deed. The buyer pays an additional 1 percent only when the price exceeds $1,000,000. Every deed also needs a Gross Income Tax form, GIT/REP-3 for New Jersey residents and GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 for nonresidents.

Appeals of an assessment go to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation in New Brunswick. Petitions can be filed online, and evidence can be uploaded up to seven calendar days before the hearing. The statewide rule is April 1, or 45 days after assessment notices are mailed, and the appeal covers value only, not the tax amount.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Old Bridge?
sections.html: Old Bridge's size means every sale is different. A cash purchase can suit an Old Bridge owner with a house that has deferred maintenance, an estate property, or a short timeline. Compare the offer to a listing net after agent fees, repairs, carrying costs and the fees above. Whoever buys, such as a family member, an investor or a cash buyer, get in writing who obtains the township approval and smoke alarm certificate and who pays for any repairs the inspection requires.

faqs.q: Does Old Bridge Township require an inspection when a house is sold?
faqs.a: Ask the township's Housing Inspection Division what applies to your address, and get its current checklist and fee in writing. Separately, state fire code requires a smoke alarm compliance certificate before a one- or two-family home is sold.

faqs.q: How long is a smoke alarm compliance certificate valid?
faqs.a: Six months from the date of issue. The Division of Fire Safety says it must be obtained through the municipality before a one- or two-family home is sold, leased or changes occupancy.

faqs.q: When must I file a property tax appeal in Old Bridge?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Board of Taxation must receive the petition by April 1, or 45 days after assessment notices are mailed, whichever is later. In a town with a recent revaluation the date is May 1. Only the assessed value can be challenged, not the tax bill.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Old Bridge?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $461,000 for owner-occupied homes for 2020 through 2024. That compares with $332,700 for the United States. Your own house will vary by neighborhood, age and condition.

faqs.q: Who pays the New Jersey 1 percent fee on a sale?
faqs.a: The buyer pays it, and only if the total price is above $1,000,000. Sellers pay the Realty Transfer Fee based on the consideration stated in the deed, with partial exemptions available for qualifying seniors, blind or disabled sellers.
